conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session September 01, 2016
conflicts.issue: Policy 4132.8 First-Day vs. Tenth-Day Magnet School Enrollment Deadline
conflicts.summary: The board split 5-1 on revising Policy 4132.8 to require magnet-school students to commit by the first day of school instead of allowing a 10-day window to return automatically to base schools, with Matt Sears dissenting in favor of family flexibility.
conflicts.side_a_position: Lock in magnet assignments on the first day of school so late moves require a special-assignment transfer.
side_a_arguments: More than 100 students leaving magnets during the first 10 days destabilize receiving and sending schools right as teacher allotments are adjusted at day 10.
Families receive lottery results in March and have open houses and orientation before day one, matching regional district best practices.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain flexibility for families during the opening days of school without imposing an extra transfer hurdle.
side_b_arguments: Roughly 100 students spread across more than 20 magnet schools is a modest number.
Requiring a formal transfer after day one adds friction against school choice if a child tries a school on the first day and finds it is not a fit.
conflicts.resolution: Policy 4132.8 revision passed 5-1 with Matt Sears opposed.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session September 01, 2016
conflicts.issue: District 2 Vacancy Criteria Ranking, Public Record Disclosure, and Interview Procedures
conflicts.summary: Board members debated how to weight school-system experience versus community leadership in the District 2 application packet, whether to hold public candidate interviews with standardized questions, and exact September deadlines.
conflicts.side_a_position: De-emphasize prior school employment in favor of public education advocacy and community leadership, disclose public-record status, and wait on deciding interview format until seeing applicant volume.
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe argued putting school-system experience at the top of the qualifications list discourages non-educator community leaders.

Minnie Forte-Brown opposed putting candidates through public job-style interviews and preferred seeing who applies first, while Xavier Cason proposed a September 20 deadline with Board of Elections verification on the 21st.
conflicts.side_b_position: Ensure transparent, standardized public interviews or Q&A and publish submitted application materials while meeting early October appointment targets.
side_b_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee argued any interviews in open session must ask every candidate the same core questions for fairness and favored a fast timeline ahead of the October 24 statutory cutoff.
Natalie Beyer favored brief follow-up Q&A on written packets and Letters of Support, while Matt Sears urged explicit public-record notice on applications and face-to-face meetings with applicants.
conflicts.resolution: The board reordered criteria to list commitment to public education advocacy first, added a public-record disclosure notice, set a September 20 deadline with September 22 public review, deferred interview format until reviewing applicants, and approved packet cleanup and outreach 6-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting August 25, 2016
conflicts.issue: Piloting Off-Site School Board Work Sessions vs. Keeping Meetings Downtown
conflicts.summary: Public commenters opposed holding work sessions at outlying high schools due to public-transit burdens, while board members unanimously backed a limited two-school pilot at Hillside and Northern High Schools using existing district equipment.
conflicts.side_a_position: Test two pilot work sessions at Hillside High School (November) and Northern High School (April) without purchasing new hardware.
side_a_arguments: Holding occasional sessions at high schools engages communities, showcases schools, and provides ample parking on bus lines.
Limiting the effort to two pilots while borrowing cameras from School for Creative Studies and reusing existing Chromebooks avoids extra spending.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep all board work sessions at the central downtown Fuller Building rather than rotating to outlying schools.
side_b_arguments: Public commenters Jackie Wagstaff and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison argued that low-income, transit-dependent residents face multiple bus transfers to reach schools outside downtown, whereas board members should visit schools individually instead.
conflicts.resolution: The board voted 6-0 to plan two pilot remote work sessions at Hillside High and Northern High.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational and Policy Work Session September 08, 2016
conflicts.issue: Necessity of Adopting Policy 2302 on Remote Participation in Board Meetings
conflicts.summary: Following intense public opposition to draft Policy 2302, board members present concluded that existing Policy 2300 already adequately permitted remote participation under exceptional circumstances and declined to advance the optional policy, contrasting with Chair Dr. Mike Lee's absent position favoring formal guidelines.
conflicts.side_a_position: Existing Policy 2300 suffices for exceptional circumstances and no separate Policy 2302 should be adopted.
side_a_arguments: Policy 2300 already requires in-person attendance while permitting telephone or electronic participation under exceptional circumstances.
Adopting a detailed standalone remote-participation policy is unnecessary and sends the wrong signal to the community.
conflicts.side_b_position: Formal written guidelines in Policy 2302 could clarify permissible circumstances such as work travel or medical recovery.
side_b_arguments: Written parameters were previously raised by Chair Dr. Mike Lee (noted by public speakers from newspaper reporting and August 11 discussion) to formalize when members with outside obligations could call in.
conflicts.resolution: No motion was made on Policy 2302; the board concluded no action was needed and moved on to the next agenda item.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 22, 2016
conflicts.issue: Allowing Live Public Comment in Support of District 2 Vacancy Candidates
conflicts.summary: During planning for the District 2 candidate forum, Chair Dr. Mike Lee proposed allowing public speakers to testify in support of applicants, while Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer opposed live support testimony as biased, time-consuming, and unnecessary given written letters of support.
conflicts.side_a_position: Allow live public comment in support of individual District 2 applicants during the candidate forum.
side_a_arguments: Community involvement and direct public input on the applicants are worth a longer meeting.
conflicts.side_b_position: Limit the candidate forum to applicant presentations and rely on written letters of support and normal community outreach.
side_b_arguments: Live cheering or support testimony introduces bias favoring candidates with larger organized followings.
Applicants already submitted two letters of support each, and public testimony for 13 candidates would make the meeting run all night.
Community members can already email or contact board members directly.
conflicts.resolution: The board proceeded without live public-support testimony during the candidate forum, scheduling candidate-only presentations on September 27 (backup October 3) and a selection vote on October 5.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education District 2 Vacancy Candidates October 3, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: In this special meeting, Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the six-member Durham Public Schools Board of Education to hear five-minute presentations from the final two applicants for the vacant District 2 seat, Nadia Porter and Christine Folch. After a moment of silence honoring school safety following a fatal shooting at a South Carolina elementary school and a unanimous 6-0 vote to approve the agenda, both candidates addressed the board's guiding principles—academic excellence, teaching the whole child, and racial and social justice—alongside teacher retention, academic achievement for boys of color, and early childhood education access. Porter focused on full-week pre-K access for Title I and IDEA students, field-trip equity and restorative discipline for boys of color, and reframing teacher retention as "teacher restoration," while Folch emphasized inclusive support for DPS's growing Hispanic (28.5%), Asian, and free-and-reduced-lunch student populations and stronger career and college pipelines with Research Triangle employers, Duke University, and North Carolina Central University. The board took no appointment vote during the session and adjourned until Wednesday, October 5 at 4:30 p.m. to vote on filling the District 2 seat.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the special meeting to order to hear from the final two applicants for the District 2 Board of Education vacancy. He led a moment of silence asking attendees to reflect on school safety and the district's duty to protect children following the recent fatal shooting of a six-year-old student at a school in South Carolina.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presented the special meeting agenda and confirmed that public comment was not included for this candidate-presentation session. A board member moved and another seconded approval of the agenda, which passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: District 2 Vacancy Candidate Presentation: Nadia Porter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Applicant Nadia Porter addressed the board's guiding principles and three focus areas, citing her daughter's experience with three-day-per-week Title I/IDEA pre-K scheduling as a barrier for low-income working families needing full-week early childhood education. She highlighted disparities in educational field trips and advocated restorative counseling for both harmed students and students causing harm rather than solely punitive discipline for young boys of color. On staffing, Porter urged replacing the framing of "teacher retention" with "teacher restoration" by surveying teachers and meeting their financial, emotional, and instructional needs.

agenda_items.title: District 2 Vacancy Candidate Presentation: Christine Folch
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Applicant Christine Folch, a Duke University professor and native Spanish speaker, discussed DPS's shifting demographics—highlighting that 28.5% of students are Hispanic—and argued that cultural and linguistic diversity in classrooms is a district strength despite resource constraints and teacher-retention pressures. She emphasized supporting educators working across cultural boundaries and connecting students before and during high school to Research Triangle businesses, workforce training, Duke University, and North Carolina Central University so students can envision post-graduation career and college pathways.

agenda_items.title: Closing Remarks and Announcement of October 5 Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee thanked both Nadia Porter and Christine Folch for their presentations. He announced that the board would reconvene on Wednesday, October 5 at 4:30 p.m. to vote on the District 2 appointment and adjourned the meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of Special Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Mover and seconder voices not identified by name in transcript; Chair declared voice vote passed unanimously by the six-member seated board.
votes.discussion_detail: Board confirmed no public comment was scheduled for this special candidate-presentation meeting before voting on the agenda as presented.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education District 2 Vacancy Candidates September 27, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At a special meeting on September 27, 2016, Chair Dr. Mike Lee and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard five-minute presentations from nine eligible applicants seeking appointment to the vacant District 2 seat. After a moment of silence reflecting on recent police killings of Black residents in Charlotte and nationwide, the board approved the meeting agenda by consensus following a motion and second and heard in succession from Pastor Frederick A. Davis, Elizabeth Ruth Lindquist, Jenna Highland, Bettina Amstead, Ann Hartman, Dr. Regina George Bowden, Cecilia Polanco, Marshall Williams, and DeWorn Langley. Candidates addressed the board's guiding principles—academic excellence, teaching the whole child, and racial and social justice—alongside teacher retention, achievement for boys of color, and early childhood education, offering proposals ranging from extended school days and disproportionate equity-based funding to urban-education teacher pipelines, mental health partnerships, and collective impact initiatives. Chair Lee noted that the final two candidates, Nadia Porter and Christine Folch, would present on Monday, October 3 at 6:30 p.m., ahead of the board's scheduled October 5 vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the special meeting to order and asked the board and audience to observe a moment of silence. He asked attendees to reflect on recent incidents in Charlotte and across the country involving police shootings of Black men and women, and to hope for peace and unity.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval and Candidate Forum Procedures
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the handout agenda for the District 2B candidate presentations after a motion and second. Chair Lee announced that two applicants—Nadia Porter and Christine Folch—had conflicts and would speak at a follow-up special meeting on Monday at 6:30 p.m., and explained that each candidate had up to five minutes to address the board's three guiding principles and three retreat focus areas.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Pastor Frederick A. Davis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Former District 2 board member (2006–2014) Frederick A. Davis cited his service dating back to the 1992 city-county school merger, his ongoing school improvement team work at Lowe's Grove Middle and Lakeview, and his advocacy for a task force to create a school for young men of color. He called for equity in rigorous coursework and hiring, sustained mentoring and scaffolding for teacher retention, and universal early childhood education supported by state funding.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Elizabeth Ruth Lindquist
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Elizabeth Ruth Lindquist urged prioritizing elementary proficiency—citing 2016 fifth-grade proficiency rates of 47% in math and 44% in reading—and proposed extending the school day by an hour to expand arts, physical education, and guided instruction while retaining funding in public schools rather than charter schools. She argued that closing the achievement gap requires authentic parent engagement and allocating funding and resources disproportionately to the students and schools with the greatest need.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Jenna Highland
agenda_items.discussion_summary: International humanitarian worker and former Atlanta Police Department juvenile crime strategist Jenna Highland emphasized her experience convening school boards, police, nonprofits, and families around hyper-local policy solutions. As an E.K. Powe parent, she committed to listening across Durham's diverse communities and applying a systemic racial and social justice lens to board policy.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Bettina Amstead
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Student U middle school program director Bettina Amstead stressed that "culture eats policy for breakfast," urging the board to back its new Student Code of Conduct, restorative practices, and anti-deportation stance with ongoing implicit bias training and direct student and family participation. She also called for continued district funding and incentives for mentor teacher programs, peer-led professional development, and teacher retention without waiting on the General Assembly.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Ann Hartman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public health nurse and nurse educator Ann Hartman linked student mental and physical health disparities—including anxiety, depression, trauma, and poverty—directly to academic achievement under the whole-child principle. Acknowledging her white privilege and racial equity training, she pledged to listen to families and board members of color and examine district policies for institutional bias harming boys of color.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Dr. Regina George Bowden
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Former eight-year DPS Board member and Vice Chair Dr. Regina George Bowden highlighted her 40-year career in education, 35 years of Latin American cultural research, and multi-generational roots in Durham schools. She recommended recruiting teachers from urban-education university programs, strengthening teacher pay and professionalism, adapting teaching styles for young men of color, and building multi-stakeholder coalitions for early childhood education; a brief audio interference pause occurred after her remarks at 00:43:22.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Cecilia Polanco
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recent UNC-Chapel Hill graduate, Northern High alumna, and small-business owner Cecilia Polanco described her path from Head Start and founding Northern's International Club to running So Good Pupusas and a scholarship initiative for undocumented students. As Northern High's first Latina student body president, she emphasized the importance of Latino representation on the board, supportive school leadership for teacher retention, and equitable opportunities regardless of socioeconomic status.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: Marshall Williams
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Marshall Williams pointed to the loss of neighborhood after-school programs and schools such as Merrick-Moore, arguing that years of board rhetoric on racial and social justice had not yielded sufficient action for African American boys. Drawing on his volunteer tutoring experience with N.C. Central students, he advocated restoring recess and physical activity alongside supportive adult mentoring.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Presentation: DeWorn Langley
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lifelong District 2 resident DeWorn Langley argued that Durham must look within and build a collective impact strategy uniting DPS, NCCU, Duke University, and nonprofits so students can benefit from Durham's economic growth. He urged collaborating directly with students, parents, teachers, and principals rather than making top-down decisions from the dais.

agenda_items.title: Closing Remarks and Next Steps
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee praised all nine candidates and noted the board would reconvene on Monday, October 3 to hear from the final two applicants. He stated that the board remained scheduled to vote on the District 2 appointment on October 5.

votes.item_title: Approval of Special Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Transcript records Chair stating the motion was moved and seconded and proceeding with the approved agenda without a formal roll call or recorded opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Lee called for a motion to approve the handout agenda for the special District 2 candidate meeting and announced it was moved and seconded before transitioning into candidate remarks.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 22, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 22, 2016 regular monthly meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved the amended agenda, August 24–25 minutes, the Policy 9000 facilities consent agenda, second-reading revisions to Policies 4132 (Student Transfers) and 4130 (School Assignment), and HVAC controls bids for the Staff Development Center and R.N. Harris Elementary. The board also unanimously added seats to the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee and appointed Emily Chávez as its community representative, selected Matt Sears, Xavier Cason, Natalie Beyer, and the forthcoming District 2 appointee as NCSBA voting delegates (with Minnie Forte-Brown as alternate), and scheduled District 2 vacancy candidate forums for September 27 (with October 3 as backup) ahead of an October 5 appointment vote. During the District 2 scheduling discussion, Chair Dr. Mike Lee favored allowing live public comment in support of candidates, whereas Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer opposed it as biased and redundant with required support letters, resulting in a forum limited to candidate presentations. Public speakers also sharply criticized the District 2 criteria and the $90 million November 2016 school bond referendum, prompting Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme to defend the bond's capital priorities for Northern High School and Eno Valley Elementary.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the regular monthly meeting, explained public comment rules, and led the board and audience in a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Celebrations and Student of the Month Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members recognized parents in attendance and honored Middle College High School student Mariann Anel Paguero Montes de Ota as Student of the Month for her academic achievement and community leadership.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme paid tribute to former DPS administrator Marvin Pittman, noted student artwork displayed at the Fuller Building, and reported that approximately 1,100 DPS students registered to vote in spring drives with more than a third of schools set to host Kids Voting elections.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A board member proposed amending the agenda after the consent agenda to add appointments to the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee and selection of voting delegates to the North Carolina School Boards Association (NCSBA) assembly. The amended agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eight residents signed up for general public comment, including Minister Paul Scott, Dr. E. Lavonia Allison, and Angelica Green. Speakers urged accountability to Black students, raised 1992 merger history regarding board representation, and criticized administrative transparency and employee free-speech concerns.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 24 and August 25, 2016 Board Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes from the August 24 and August 25, 2016 Board of Education meetings. A motion to approve the minutes was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Policy 9000 Series (Facilities)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Lee noted that the Policy 9000 facilities series was the sole item on the consent agenda. The consent agenda was moved, seconded, and approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Zero-Based Budgeting Committee Additions and Appointment of Emily Chávez
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears presented a proposal to add three seats to the newly formed Zero-Based Budgeting Committee (including an additional principal seat to be filled by administration) and nominated Emily Chávez as the board-appointed community representative. The board unanimously approved both the additional seats and Chávez's appointment.

agenda_items.title: Selection of North Carolina School Boards Association (NCSBA) Voting Delegates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Minnie Forte-Brown explained the NCSBA legislative agenda survey and delegate assembly scheduled for November 16–18 in Greensboro, where DPS holds four delegate votes. Because Forte-Brown is an NCSBA officer and ineligible to serve as a delegate, the board confirmed Matt Sears, Xavier Cason, Natalie Beyer, and the incoming District 2 appointee (TBD) as delegates—with Forte-Brown as alternate—by acclamation.

agenda_items.title: District 2 Vacancy Applicant Verification and Hearing/Vote Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following sharp public comments from Dr. Anita Keith-Foust, Jackie Wagstaff, and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison invoking the 1992 merger compromise and challenging the board's candidate criteria, Chair Dr. Mike Lee announced that 13 applicants had submitted packets to be posted online the next morning, with Shonda Wilson and Florida DeVaughn Dudley disqualified for living outside District 2 and Jenna Highland pending Board of Elections address verification. Board members disagreed over allowing live public testimony for candidates—with Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer overriding Chair Lee's suggestion in favor of letters of support—and agreed by acclamation to hear candidates on September 27 (backup October 3) and vote on October 5 at 4:30 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Update on the 2016 School Bond Referendum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers Dr. Anita Keith-Foust, Jackie Wagstaff, and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison opposed the $90 million November 8 school bond, alleging inequitable past allocations to Black schools, unaddressed maintenance at Eastway Elementary, unused land holdings such as the $4.1 million Duke Homestead parcel, and prior bond fund transfers. Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme responded that $90 million was approved from a $186 million request, prioritizing Northern High School replacement (82% students of color) and Eno Valley Elementary (95% students of color), cited endorsements from Friends of Durham, People's Alliance, and the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People, and clarified that bond funds are restricted by law to capital projects rather than textbooks.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Report: Policies 4132 (Student Transfers), 4130 (School Assignment), and 4131 (Magnet Schools)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented second-reading updates to Policy 4132 (Student Transfers) and Policy 4130 (School Assignment) for formal adoption, noting Policy 4131 (Magnet Schools) remained informational only. The board unanimously adopted Policies 4132 and 4130.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Report: HVAC Controls Replacement Bids (Staff Development Center and R.N. Harris Elementary)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following up from the Operational Services and Policy Work Session, the board reviewed the HVAC controls replacement bids for the Staff Development Center and R.N. Harris Elementary. A motion to approve the bids passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and voted unanimously to enter closed session to approve closed-session minutes, consider confidential personnel matters under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and 115C-319, and consult with the board attorney under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), with Chair Lee advising attendees that open-session business had concluded.

votes.item_title: Amend and Approve September 22, 2016 Agenda
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not explicitly named in transcript; voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Added Zero-Based Budgeting Committee member additions and NCSBA voting delegate elections immediately following the consent agenda.

votes.item_title: Approve August 24 and August 25, 2016 Board Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: No corrections or discussion raised on the August 24 and August 25, 2016 minutes.

votes.item_title: Zero-Based Budgeting Committee Additional Seats and Appointment of Emily Chávez
votes.notes: Presented by Matt Sears; voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved three additional seats on the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee (including an administrative principal appointment) and appointed Emily Chávez as the board's community representative.

votes.item_title: Designate NCSBA Delegate Assembly Representatives
votes.discussion_detail: Selected Matt Sears, Xavier Cason, Natalie Beyer, and the forthcoming District 2 appointee as the four voting delegates for the November 16–18 NCSBA assembly, with Minnie Forte-Brown as alternate.

votes.item_title: Set District 2 Vacancy Candidate Hearing and Selection Vote Schedule
votes.notes: Approved by acclamation after calendar coordination.
votes.discussion_detail: Agreed to hear District 2 applicants on September 27 (with October 3 as backup) and hold a special called meeting on October 5 at 4:30 p.m. to vote on the appointment.

votes.item_title: Second-Reading Adoption of Policy 4132 (Student Transfers) and Policy 4130 (School Assignment)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Policies 4132 and 4130 on second reading following prior work-session approval; Policy 4131 remained informational.

votes.item_title: Approve Staff Development Center and R.N. Harris Elementary HVAC Controls Bids
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the HVAC controls replacement bids for the Staff Development Center and R.N. Harris Elementary as forwarded from the Operational Services work session.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session (Minutes, Personnel, and Attorney-Client Consultation)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), 115C-319, and 143-318.11(a)(3) and concluded public business.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational and Policy Work Session September 08, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: With Board Chair Dr. Mike Lee absent, Operational Services and Policy Committee Chair Xavier Cason presided over the September 8, 2016 work session, where the five attending members unanimously approved moving a FERPA closed session ahead of operations items, the August 11 minutes, 2007 bond fund transfers, forwarding Staff Development Center and R.N. Harris HVAC controls contracts to the September action agenda, and forwarding five updated Policy 9000 facilities policies to the September consent agenda. The board also reached consensus for staff to form a working group with Durham County staff—with members Matt Sears and Natalie Beyer urging elected-official representation—to study recurring annual local capital funding beyond the county's $1.37 million allocation. Policy 2302 on remote meeting participation drew sharp opposition from public speakers and skepticism from Xavier Cason, Minnie Forte-Brown, and Natalie Beyer, who noted Policy 2300 already covers exceptional remote attendance; the item closed with no action taken. In closing informational updates, TNTP presented a Kenan Charitable Trust-funded Community Engagement Diagnostic Tool, and administration reviewed ESL Resource Center capacity and immigration enforcement guidance for schools after Wilden Acosta's return to Riverside High School.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding committee chair Xavier Cason opened the work session at 4:32 p.m. with a moment of silence. On a motion by Natalie Beyer seconded by Matt Sears, the board voted 5-0 (with Chair Dr. Mike Lee absent) to move closed session immediately after public comment and limit it strictly to FERPA student information.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 11, 2016 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approval of the August 11, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session minutes. The motion passed unanimously, 5-0.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jackie Wagstaff criticized the District 2 vacancy criteria as biased and inconsistent with statutory candidate requirements and the 1992 merger compromise; Dr. Anita Keith-Foust condemned the return of the remote participation policy to the agenda; and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison protested moving closed session ahead of public presentations, limiting speakers to two topics, and Chairman Lee's newspaper remarks on remote participation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Student Information / FERPA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer moved and Steve Unruhe seconded entering closed session under N.C.G.S. 115C-402 and FERPA (20 U.S.C. 1232g). The motion passed 5-0, and the board returned to open session at 00:16:19.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services 6A: 2007 Bond Fund Transfers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Dr. E. Lavonia Allison questioned the rationale for shifting 2007 bond balances—including $100,000 for Northern High School and $235,474 for HVAC—staff explained the net-zero closeout transfers left roughly $600,000 unspent, funding bleachers at School for Creative Studies and Githens Middle, pre-bond consultant work for Northern High, and HVAC controls. Matt Sears moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approval of the 2007 bond transfers, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services 6B: HVAC Controls Replacement Bids (R.N. Harris and Staff Development Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported three bids received August 11 for HVAC controls work at R.N. Harris Elementary and the Staff Development Center, recommending apparent low bidder CMS Controls with preferred-brand alternates 1A, 1B, 2A, and 2C added at no cost change. Matt Sears moved and Steve Unruhe seconded placing the revised HVAC contracts on the September full board action agenda, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services 6C: Local Annual Capital Outlay Study Group
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff highlighted that DPS receives only $1.37 million annually in county non-bond local capital outlay for nearly 6 million square feet of facilities (plus lottery funds from which the county retains $1 million for debt service) and proposed a joint DPS-county staff group to recommend sustainable recurring capital funding. Xavier Cason, Matt Sears, and Natalie Beyer supported the study and urged including elected school board members and county commissioners on the group, concluding by consensus with no formal vote.

agenda_items.title: Policy 9000 Series Facilities Revisions (Policies 9000, 9010, 9020, 9030, and 9110)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented five updated facilities policies—9000 (Planning), 9010 (Site Selection), 9020 (Facility Design), 9030 (Quality of Construction and monthly change-order reporting), and 9110 (Professional Services Selection thresholds at $50,000 and $90,000)—to prepare for the 2016 bond and align with state statutes. After Natalie Beyer asked about environmental sustainability standards and staff confirmed sustainability language was embedded, Steve Unruhe moved and a colleague seconded placing the five policies on the September regular meeting consent agenda, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Policy 2302: Remote Participation in Board Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers Jackie Wagstaff, Dr. Anita Keith-Foust, and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison strongly opposed Policy 2302, arguing elected members must attend in person and warning against enabling absences. Xavier Cason cited existing Policy 2300 as already allowing conference-call participation under exceptional circumstances, and Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer agreed no new policy was needed, ending the item with no action.

agenda_items.title: TNTP Community Engagement Diagnostic Tool Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme and TNTP representatives Leticia de la Vara and Wesley Bias presented a Community Engagement Diagnostic Tool fully funded by the Kenan Charitable Trust to assess district, school, and classroom engagement through data analysis, interviews, and focus groups through calendar year-end. Board members questioned geographic disaggregation, stakeholder identification, and how state constraints like the elimination of tenure and master's pay would be addressed, before Chair Cason departed at 01:32:58 for another meeting and passed the gavel.

agenda_items.title: Immigration and Refugee Student Support and Follow-Up Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration reviewed services for approximately 4,650 ESL-eligible students—noting the ESL Resource Center is outgrowing the Staff Development Center—alongside mental health partnerships with El Futuro and Carolina Outreach and updated federal/district guidance against immigration enforcement on school campuses. Board members discussed support for unschooled refugee youth, teacher-level clarity on student rights following Wilden Acosta's return to Riverside High School, smooth opening-week transportation under the new bell schedule, and Geer Road apartment bus access before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Amend and Approve Agenda (Move Closed Session After Public Comment; FERPA Only)
votes.notes: Chair Dr. Mike Lee was absent (confirmed by public commenters at 00:11:23 and 00:13:52).
votes.discussion_detail: Moved closed session (item 10) between items 5 and 6 after public comment and struck the first two closed-session statutory grounds, keeping only FERPA student information.

votes.item_title: Approve August 11, 2016 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: No edits or objections raised to the August 11, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session minutes.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session (Confidential Student Information / FERPA)
votes.notes: Dr. Mike Lee absent; board returned to open session at 00:16:19.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 115C-402 and FERPA (20 U.S.C. 1232g) immediately following general public comment.

votes.item_title: Approve 2007 Bond Fund Transfers
votes.discussion_detail: Approved net-zero closeout transfers of remaining 2007 bond funds toward middle school gym bleachers (SCS and Githens), Northern High School pre-bond consulting ($100,000), and HVAC controls ($235,474).

votes.item_title: Place HVAC Controls Replacement Bids on September Regular Meeting Action Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: Forwarded R.N. Harris Elementary and Staff Development Center HVAC controls contracts (apparent low bidder CMS Controls, adding preferred-brand alternates at no cost change) to the September full board action agenda.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational and Policy Work Session September 08, 2016
disagreements.issue: Necessity of Adopting Policy 2302 on Remote Participation in Board Meetings
disagreements.summary: Following intense public opposition to draft Policy 2302, board members present concluded that existing Policy 2300 already adequately permitted remote participation under exceptional circumstances and declined to advance the optional policy, contrasting with Chair Dr. Mike Lee's absent position favoring formal guidelines.
disagreements.side_a_position: Existing Policy 2300 suffices for exceptional circumstances and no separate Policy 2302 should be adopted.
side_a_arguments: Policy 2300 already requires in-person attendance while permitting telephone or electronic participation under exceptional circumstances.
Adopting a detailed standalone remote-participation policy is unnecessary and sends the wrong signal to the community.
disagreements.side_b_position: Formal written guidelines in Policy 2302 could clarify permissible circumstances such as work travel or medical recovery.
side_b_arguments: Written parameters were previously raised by Chair Dr. Mike Lee (noted by public speakers from newspaper reporting and August 11 discussion) to formalize when members with outside obligations could call in.
disagreements.resolution: No motion was made on Policy 2302; the board concluded no action was needed and moved on to the next agenda item.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session September 01, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 1, 2016 Academic and Student Services Work Session, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education approved an NCCU memorandum of agreement, four major instructional software and curriculum contracts (Edmentum, Curriculum Associates i-Ready, Discovery Education, and Learning A-Z), preliminary 2015–16 accountability data review, updates to student transfer and assignment policies (4132 and 4130), and the public application process for filling the vacant District 2 seat. With Minnie Forte-Brown arriving late at 00:49:28, the first four procedural and NCCU items passed 5-0, and the four instructional contracts and most policy revisions passed 6-0. On Policy 4132.8, however, the board split 5-1—with Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Minnie Forte-Brown, Xavier Cason, and Steve Unruhe voting Aye and Matt Sears voting Nay—to require magnet students wishing to return to base schools to lock in their choice by the first day of school rather than the tenth day. Board members also debated how to structure District 2 vacancy qualifications, public disclosure, and candidate interviews before approving a September 20 application deadline, public record disclosure, outreach flyers and robocalls, and document cleanup by Natalie Beyer.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Amended Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the work session to order and led a moment of silence. Because Minnie Forte-Brown would arrive late, the board amended and approved the agenda 5-0 to add an immediate closed session on student information, move contracts ahead of data reports, add a District 2 vacancy process discussion, and add a closing closed session on personnel and student matters.

agenda_items.title: Initial Closed Session (Student Information and Personnel)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to 20 U.S.C. 1232g and N.C.G.S. 115C-402. Upon returning to open session at 00:43:08, Chair Lee amended the public record to note that personnel matters under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and 115C-319 were also discussed.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 4, 2016 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the Academic and Student Services Work Session minutes from August 4, 2016. A motion to approve the minutes passed unanimously, 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Memorandum of Agreement with North Carolina Central University (NCCU)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an updated Memorandum of Agreement with North Carolina Central University recommended by the board attorney for immediate execution. The board voted 5-0 to approve the agreement, immediately after which Minnie Forte-Brown joined the meeting at 00:49:28.

agenda_items.title: Edmentum Three-Year Contract (Plato Credit Recovery, EdOptions Academy, and CTE Courses)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a three-year Edmentum contract covering Plato district-wide credit recovery ($75,000 already budgeted, replacing Apex), EdOptions Academy for flexible mid-year enrollment, and 50 online CTE supplemental courses with nine professional development days. Board members requested teacher perception and outcome tracking beyond login counts, then unanimously approved the contract over $90,000 by a 6-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Curriculum Associates Contract (i-Ready Screener and Read to Achieve Teacher Toolbox)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested renewal of the sole-source Curriculum Associates i-Ready universal screener for grades 3–8 math and 4–8 reading (nearly $300,000 across local/federal funds) paired with a K–2 and 6–8 Teacher Toolbox funded by leftover Read to Achieve summer camp state dollars. After questions from Steve Unruhe and Natalie Beyer about teacher survey feedback and cost-saving negotiations, the board approved the contract 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Discovery Education Contract Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff sought approval of a $148,000 sole-source local-funded renewal for Discovery Education, noting more than 25,000 individual users with three or more logins, elementary virtual field trips linked to a nine-point elementary science gain, and snow-day assignment continuity via Board Builder. After discussion on sales tax rules and measuring student achievement impact, the board approved the contract 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Learning A-Z Contract Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a K–5 sole-source renewal of Learning A-Z (including Reading A-Z, Science A-Z, and Raz-Kids) fully funded by leftover Read to Achieve summer camp state dollars at no local cost. Board members discussed home and mobile access, public library/community center access for families without internet, classroom device needs, and pairing teacher survey and longitudinal reading data with usage metrics before voting 6-0 to approve.

agenda_items.title: 2015–16 Preliminary State Accountability Data Release and Progress Monitoring Platform
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme and Dr. Spencer reviewed preliminary 2015–16 EOG/EOC data released that morning, highlighting 100% graduation rates at Middle College, JD Clement Early College, and City of Medicine Academy, A+ grades at Mangum, Early College, and City of Medicine, gains in 27 of 30 elementary schools, and district-wide college-and-career readiness of 36.3% (44.9% grade-level proficient), alongside persistent gaps in middle school, English II, and math course rigor. Board members criticized punitive state A–F letter grades, requested disaggregated learning and subgroup data, and welcomed staff's proposed year-round progress-monitoring schedule (October elementary, November middle, December high school, January ELL, February boys of color, March advanced academics).

agenda_items.title: Policy 4132 (Student Transfers), Policy 4130 (School Assignment), and Policy 4131 (Magnet Schools) Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office of Student Assignment Director Donna Hudson presented three updates to Policy 4132 and an alignment update to Policy 4130, plus informational data on secondary sibling links under Policy 4131. The board unanimously (6-0) eliminated the mandatory opt-out transfer form for Easley and Holt year-round base zones (4132.5), authorized administrative hardship waivers for missed calendar-magnet lottery deadlines (4132.6), and aligned Policy 4130, while splitting 5-1 (Matt Sears dissenting) on Policy 4132.8 to move the magnet-to-base return deadline from the 10th day to the first day of school.

agenda_items.title: District 2 Vacancy Application Process, Timeline, and Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With a 60-day statutory deadline of October 24 to replace Sendolo Diaminah, board members debated candidate qualification rankings, public disclosure of submitted materials, and whether to conduct standardized public interviews. The board adopted a September 20 application deadline (with Board of Elections verification on September 21 and public review on September 22), voted 6-0 to empower Vice Chair Natalie Beyer to finalize the edited packet, and voted 6-0 to authorize Chair Lee to oversee multi-channel outreach including Spanish translation, robocalls, and 33,000 flyers.

agenda_items.title: Closing Closed Session (Student Information, Personnel, and Attorney-Client)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and voted 6-0 to enter closed session on confidential student information (20 U.S.C. 1232g; G.S. 115C-402), personnel (G.S. 115C-319; 143-318.11(a)(6)), and attorney-client privilege (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)).

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the August 4, 2016 work session minutes without modification.

votes.discussion_detail: Executed updated Memorandum of Agreement with NCCU following board attorney review.

votes.item_title: Approve Curriculum Associates Contract (i-Ready Screener and Toolbox)
votes.notes: All six seated board members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved sole-source i-Ready screener and Read to Achieve-funded Teacher Toolbox renewal ahead of October 1 license expiration.

votes.item_title: Approve Discovery Education Contract Renewal
votes.notes: All six seated board members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved $148,000 sole-source K–12 digital curriculum and Board Builder contract funded locally.

votes.item_title: Approve Learning A-Z Contract Renewal
votes.notes: All six seated board members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved K–5 Reading A-Z, Science A-Z, and Raz-Kids contract funded entirely with remaining state Read to Achieve summer camp funds.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session September 01, 2016
disagreements.issue: Policy 4132.8 First-Day vs. Tenth-Day Magnet School Enrollment Deadline
disagreements.summary: The board split 5-1 on revising Policy 4132.8 to require magnet-school students to commit by the first day of school instead of allowing a 10-day window to return automatically to base schools, with Matt Sears dissenting in favor of family flexibility.
disagreements.side_a_position: Lock in magnet assignments on the first day of school so late moves require a special-assignment transfer.
side_a_arguments: More than 100 students leaving magnets during the first 10 days destabilize receiving and sending schools right as teacher allotments are adjusted at day 10.
Families receive lottery results in March and have open houses and orientation before day one, matching regional district best practices.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain flexibility for families during the opening days of school without imposing an extra transfer hurdle.
side_b_arguments: Roughly 100 students spread across more than 20 magnet schools is a modest number.
Requiring a formal transfer after day one adds friction against school choice if a child tries a school on the first day and finds it is not a fit.
disagreements.resolution: Policy 4132.8 revision passed 5-1 with Matt Sears opposed.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Academic & Student Services Work Session September 01, 2016
disagreements.issue: District 2 Vacancy Criteria Ranking, Public Record Disclosure, and Interview Procedures
disagreements.summary: Board members debated how to weight school-system experience versus community leadership in the District 2 application packet, whether to hold public candidate interviews with standardized questions, and exact September deadlines.
disagreements.side_a_position: De-emphasize prior school employment in favor of public education advocacy and community leadership, disclose public-record status, and wait on deciding interview format until seeing applicant volume.
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe argued putting school-system experience at the top of the qualifications list discourages non-educator community leaders.

Minnie Forte-Brown opposed putting candidates through public job-style interviews and preferred seeing who applies first, while Xavier Cason proposed a September 20 deadline with Board of Elections verification on the 21st.
disagreements.side_b_position: Ensure transparent, standardized public interviews or Q&A and publish submitted application materials while meeting early October appointment targets.
side_b_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee argued any interviews in open session must ask every candidate the same core questions for fairness and favored a fast timeline ahead of the October 24 statutory cutoff.
Natalie Beyer favored brief follow-up Q&A on written packets and Letters of Support, while Matt Sears urged explicit public-record notice on applications and face-to-face meetings with applicants.
disagreements.resolution: The board reordered criteria to list commitment to public education advocacy first, added a public-record disclosure notice, set a September 20 deadline with September 22 public review, deferred interview format until reviewing applicants, and approved packet cleanup and outreach 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting August 25, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 25, 2016 regular monthly meeting, District 2 board member Sendolo Diaminah formally resigned—effective immediately—to focus on grassroots organizing and urged the board to appoint a deeply rooted Latino community member to fill the historic representation gap. Operating thereafter as a six-member board under Chair Dr. Mike Lee, members unanimously (6-0) approved the amended agenda, June 23 minutes, moving the May 25, 2017 monthly meeting to May 24 due to four high school graduations, a minority-owned contract transportation renewal, shifting 2016–17 work session start times from 4:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m., appointing Durham CAN's Shannon Pickett as the seventh member of the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee, and entering closed session. Public speakers raised urgent concerns over contracted school-nursing continuity for medically fragile EC children, student voter registration demographics, and District 2 appointment fairness. Despite opposition from Jackie Wagstaff and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison to holding meetings outside downtown transit hubs, the board also voted 6-0 to pilot two remote work sessions at Hillside High School and Northern High School while trimming proposed equipment purchases by reusing district cameras and Chromebooks.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the monthly meeting to order and led a moment of silence. During celebrations, the board recognized School for Creative Studies Student of the Month and Hillside High School track alumnus Marcus Crawford, presenting a mayoral proclamation for his 2016 IAAF World Junior Championships success.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Bert L'Homme highlighted district restorative practices training and declining short-term suspensions, congratulated Chief Financial Officer Aaron Beaulieu and his team on earning all three state and national financial reporting awards (one of 12 districts statewide), noted recent grant awards, and wished Paralympian Desmond Jackson (Minnie Forte-Brown's nephew) well in Rio.

agenda_items.title: Resignation of District 2 Board Member Sendolo Diaminah and Statutory Vacancy Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before agenda review, Sendolo Diaminah formally resigned from the District 2 seat to devote himself full-time to Black movement-building and electoral organizing, urging the board to appoint a deeply rooted member of Durham's Latino immigrant community (noting Latino students make up 28.5% of DPS enrollment with zero Latino elected officials in Durham). Fellow board members praised Diaminah's moral leadership, and Board Attorney Ken Soo explained under Policy 2115 and the 1992 merger law that the board has 60 days in open session to appoint a District 2 resident before responsibility passes to County Commissioners and then the Clerk of Court.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members amended the agenda to add jointly selecting a seventh member for the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee, approving June 23, 2016 meeting minutes, and adding a FERPA closed-session ground. The amended agenda passed unanimously, 6-0.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eight speakers addressed the board: pediatric nursing representatives and parents (Mary Rollins Hughes, Jennifer Brodrick, Cynthia Bayes's statement, Julie Lynn, Stephanie Tumor, and LPN Pamela Reiser) urged waivers allowing existing CAP/C home-health nurses (PSA and Bayada) to care for medically fragile EC students in school rather than an unstaffed new contractor (Delta-T Group); Kevin and Denine Hinton sought rule relief for School for Creative Studies athletes to compete at base high schools; Minister Paul Scott announced a People's Oversight Commission; Dr. Anita Keith-Foust requested CTE trade-apprenticeship data; Dr. E. Lavonia Allison requested school-by-school demographics of 17- and 18-year-old potential voters; and Jackie Wagstaff criticized Diaminah's attendance record and urged an unbiased District 2 appointment.

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 23, 2016 Board Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the June 23, 2016 regular meeting minutes added during agenda review. A motion to approve the minutes passed unanimously, 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Reschedule May 25, 2017 Regular Board Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because four early/middle college high schools were scheduled to hold graduations on Thursday, May 25, 2017, the board proposed moving the May 2017 meeting to Wednesday, May 24, 2017. After Minnie Forte-Brown noted Wednesday evening church obligations (while acknowledging Tuesday Bible study conflicts too), the board voted 6-0 to move the meeting to May 24, 2017.

agenda_items.title: Contract Transportation Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operational Services staff presented the RFP and attached contract renewing outlier student transportation with two local Durham minority-owned firms. A motion to approve the contract transportation renewal passed unanimously, 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Pilot Remote Board Work Sessions and Work Session Start Time
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public opposition from Jackie Wagstaff and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison over bus-transfer hardships for transit-dependent residents, staff presented logistics for two pilot work sessions at high schools (November 10 and April 3). After Chair Lee and board members insisted on borrowing existing cameras from the School for Creative Studies and reusing board Chromebooks instead of spending $5,000 on new equipment, the board voted 6-0 to direct staff to plan two pilot remote work sessions (Hillside High in November and Northern High in April 2017) and voted 6-0 in a separate motion to move all 2016–17 work session start times from 4:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Appointment of Seventh Member to Zero-Based Budgeting Committee (Shannon Pickett)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Sendolo Diaminah's resignation leaving a seventh community-at-large slot on the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee, board members endorsed Durham CAN representative Shannon Pickett for her community breadth and budget experience. The board voted 6-0 to appoint Pickett to the committee.

agenda_items.title: Voter Registration Precincts and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Minnie Forte-Brown commended the addition of three school polling precincts and urged notifying schools about nearby early voting and student voter-registration materials required in media centers. The board then voted 6-0 to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda.

votes.item_title: Amend and Approve August 25, 2016 Monthly Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Taken by the six remaining seated members immediately after Sendolo Diaminah's resignation.
votes.discussion_detail: Added joint selection of a seventh Zero-Based Budgeting Committee member, June 23, 2016 minutes, and a FERPA closed-session ground.

votes.item_title: Approve June 23, 2016 Board Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the June 23, 2016 meeting minutes added to the agenda.

votes.item_title: Reschedule May 25, 2017 Board Meeting to May 24, 2017
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous after brief discussion of Wednesday vs. Tuesday church schedules.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved the May 2017 regular meeting from Thursday, May 25 to Wednesday, May 24 to avoid conflicts with four high school graduations.

votes.item_title: Approve Contract Transportation Renewal
votes.discussion_detail: Approved renewal of outlier student transportation contracts with two local minority-owned Durham firms following legal review.

votes.item_title: Direct Staff to Plan Two Pilot Remote Board Work Sessions (Hillside High and Northern High)
votes.discussion_detail: Directed staff to investigate and plan two pilot work sessions hosted at Hillside High School in November 2016 and Northern High School in April 2017 using existing district equipment.

votes.item_title: Change 2016–17 Work Session Start Times from 4:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved work session start times to 4:30 p.m. so high school teachers dismissed at 4:00 p.m. and working families have a better opportunity to attend; board also informally agreed to accommodate public comment sign-ups arriving by 4:45 p.m.

votes.item_title: Appoint Shannon Pickett to Seventh Seat on Zero-Based Budgeting Committee
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Shannon Pickett (affiliated with Durham CAN) to fill the seventh board-appointed seat on the Zero-Based Budgeting Committee.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for the statutory reasons stated on the amended agenda.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting August 25, 2016
disagreements.issue: Piloting Off-Site School Board Work Sessions vs. Keeping Meetings Downtown
disagreements.summary: Public commenters opposed holding work sessions at outlying high schools due to public-transit burdens, while board members unanimously backed a limited two-school pilot at Hillside and Northern High Schools using existing district equipment.
disagreements.side_a_position: Test two pilot work sessions at Hillside High School (November) and Northern High School (April) without purchasing new hardware.
side_a_arguments: Holding occasional sessions at high schools engages communities, showcases schools, and provides ample parking on bus lines.
Limiting the effort to two pilots while borrowing cameras from School for Creative Studies and reusing existing Chromebooks avoids extra spending.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep all board work sessions at the central downtown Fuller Building rather than rotating to outlying schools.
side_b_arguments: Public commenters Jackie Wagstaff and Dr. E. Lavonia Allison argued that low-income, transit-dependent residents face multiple bus transfers to reach schools outside downtown, whereas board members should visit schools individually instead.
disagreements.resolution: The board voted 6-0 to plan two pilot remote work sessions at Hillside High and Northern High.
